title: Comprehensive Budgeting, Procurement, Contracts, and Revenue Recognition Playbook (Q4 2024)
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Summary:
This playbook describes Redwood Inference’s end-to-end processes and controls for quarterly budgeting and forecasting, procurement approvals and vendor onboarding, contract lifecycle management, and revenue recognition/billing policies. It is intended for finance, legal, procurement owners, product and engineering managers who consume or approve budget and contract requests.

Scope:
- Applies to all departments and legal entities of Redwood Inference globally.
- Covers: annual/quarterly budget cycle, re-forecast cadence, procurement approval matrix, vendor onboarding checklist, standard contract workflow and templates, revenue recognition rules for hosted, dedicated, and private products, and billing/invoicing practices.

Definitions:
- Forecast: rolling 12-month plan updated quarterly.
- Budget: annual plan approved by the Executive Team and Board.
- Deferred revenue: cash received for services not yet delivered.
- SOW: Statement of Work.

1) Budgeting & Forecasting (quarterly cycle)
Overview:
We operate a top-down and bottoms-up budgeting process with quarterly re-forecasts. Finance provides consolidated guidance, and team leads submit detailed asks in the Budget Workbook (Sheets).

Owners and timeline:
1. Finance (owner: Head of FP&A) — issues guidance and targets (T-6 weeks before quarter start).
2. Department leads — submit detailed budgets and headcount plans (T-4 to T-3 weeks).
3. Finance — consolidation, variance analysis, and reconciliation (T-2 weeks).
4. CFO & Executive Team — review and approve final plan (T-1 week).

Deliverables:
- Budget Workbook (cost centers, headcount, GTM spend)
- Consolidated P&L, cash flow and headcount plan
- Forecast narrative covering material changes and risks

Process (detailed steps):
1. Guidance issued: growth assumptions, model pricing changes, hiring ceilings, and capital spend thresholds.
2. Inputs due: teams upload line-item budgets with owners and justification.
3. Finance consolidates and runs scenario analysis (base / downside / upside).
4. Executive review: prioritized funding decisions and re-allocations.
5. Board packet: final budget and 12-month forecast for Board review (when applicable).

Control points and approvals:
- Any incremental recurring spend > $50k/year requires Exec sponsor and Finance sign-off.
- Headcount hires beyond approved headcount plan require People Ops + Finance approval.

2) Procurement procedures and vendor onboarding
Objectives:
Ensure cost control, vendor risk assessment, and compliant contracting.

Approval thresholds (quick reference table):
- <$5,000: Manager approval (email record)
- $5,000 - $50,000: Finance approval + Procurement notification
- $50,000 - $250,000: Finance approval + Procurement + Legal review
- >$250,000 or contract term > 12 months: CFO approval + Legal + Procurement committee

Procedure (step-by-step):
1. Raise a purchase request in the Procurement portal with justification, budget code, and vendor details.
2. Procurement validates vendor (KYC, AML checks where applicable) and requests W-9 / tax documents for US vendors.
3. For software/hardware, attach license terms or SKU list and expected start/end dates.
4. Obtain approvals according to the threshold table. Approvals must be recorded in the procurement system.
5. Legal engages for contract review if required by the threshold or vendor type.
6. Finance verifies budget availability and issues a PO (if applicable).
7. Vendor onboarding checklist: insurance certificates, data processing agreement if vendor handles customer data, security questionnaire (SSQ), and payment terms.

Standard payment terms and vendor lifecycle:
- Default: Net 30 for approved vendors. Exceptions require Finance approval.
- Preferred payment method: ACH.
- Vendor master data is maintained by Procurement; changes require dual control.

3) Contracts and legal process (lifecycle)
Principles:
- Use approved Redwood templates for standard SaaS, reseller, and MSA agreements to reduce negotiation cycles.
- Legal must review non-standard clauses: indemnity caps, data residency, export controls, and security obligations.

Lifecycle steps:
1. Request: Business owner fills Contract Request Form (CRF) capturing scope, commercial terms, and risk flags.
2. Draft: Start from the relevant template in the Contract Library; the template carries approved negotiable ranges.
3. Legal review: Legal triages risk and coordinates redlines. For unusual customer terms, Legal prepares an exceptions memo.
4. Negotiation: Business owner and Legal coordinate with customer/vendor; commercial concessions logged in the CRM.
5. Signature: For contract value ≤ $250k, authorized signatory from Sales or Ops may sign; for > $250k, CFO signature required.
6. Storage & indexing: Signed contracts uploaded to Contract Repository (doc-store.redwood) with metadata (contract_owner, start_date, end_date, auto_renew_flag).

Retention and audit:
- Contracts are retained for a minimum of 7 years unless legal instructs otherwise.
- Legal conducts annual sample audits of executed contracts for compliance with approved templates.

Templates and playbooks available:
- Standard SaaS MSA (template id: MSA-2024-v2)
- Professional Services SOW (template id: SOW-PS-2023)
- Data Processing Addendum (DPA-2022)

4) Revenue recognition and billing policies
Accounting framework:
- Revenue policies follow ASC 606 / IFRS 15 principles: identify contracts, performance obligations, transaction price, allocate price and recognize revenue as obligations are satisfied.

Product-specific rules:
- Hosted API (usage-based): Recognize revenue when services are delivered (metered usage) — revenue recorded in the period usage occurred. Monthly invoices are generated in arrears.
- Dedicated and Private (capacity or subscription): Recurring subscription fees are recognized ratably over the service period. If payments are received in advance, record Deferred Revenue and amortize monthly.
- One-time professional services: Recognize revenue upon delivery of the agreed milestone or completion of the SOW, consistent with contract terms. Certain long-term engagements may require % completion accounting — coordinate with Accounting.

Billing and invoicing practices:
- Standard cadence: Monthly invoicing in arrears for usage and subscription; Annual pre-paid contracts invoice up-front with proration rules documented in the CRM.
- Invoice SLA: Invoices for closed periods are issued within 2 business days of period close.
- Payment terms: Net 30 standard; exceptions: Net 45 or Net 60 requires Finance approval and documented credit assessment.
- Credits and disputes: Customer disputes must be logged in Billing Console; credits approved by Billing Manager and Finance. Dispute resolution target: initial response within 5 business days, resolution within 10 business days.

Example journal entries (described):
- Customer prepays $120,000 for 12 months subscription on Jan 1: Dr Cash $120,000; Cr Deferred Revenue $120,000. Monthly recognition (Jan): Dr Deferred Revenue $10,000; Cr Revenue $10,000.

Controls and segregation of duties:
- Billing generation automated by Billing Service (billing-api); manual invoice adjustments require dual approval (Billing Manager + Finance).
- Revenue entries reviewed monthly by Accounting and signed off by Head of Accounting.

5) Controls, audits, and KPIs
Key controls:
- Budget owners must attest quarterly to material variances (>10% line-item).
- Procurement approval matrix enforced in the procurement portal; exceptions require an audit trail.
- Legal must sign off on any contract deviation from template negotiable ranges.

KPIs and targets:
- Invoice accuracy: 99.5% (target)
- Average time to issue invoice: ≤ 2 business days after close
- Contract turnaround time (standard MSA): target ≤ 7 business days
- Time to vendor onboarding: target ≤ 10 business days (from request to active vendor)

Audit cadence:
- Internal audit: annual review of procurement and contracting controls.
- External audit: as part of year-end financial audit, revrec and billing processes will be tested.

6) Escalation and exceptions
- Procurement exceptions: Procurement Manager -> Head of Procurement -> CFO.
- Contract exceptions (material legal risk): Legal Counsel -> General Counsel -> CEO if required.
- Revenue recognition judgment calls (percent complete, contract modifications): Head of Accounting -> CFO -> External auditor consult if unresolved.

Appendix A — Approval matrix (text table)
| Amount range | Approver(s) | Additional requirements |
|---------------|-------------|-------------------------|
| <$5k | Manager | Email approval, PO optional |
| $5k-$50k | Finance | Create PO; procurement notified |
| $50k-$250k | Finance + Procurement + Legal | Contract template review |
| >$250k | CFO + Legal + Procurement committee | Board notification if strategic |

Appendix B — Vendor onboarding checklist (bullet list)
- Completed vendor intake form
- W-9 / W-8BEN or local tax docs
- Insurance certificate (general liability)
- SSQ / security assessment if vendor handles customer data
- Signed DPA if required
- Bank details and ACH set-up verified

Review cadence:
This playbook is reviewed annually or when material policy changes occur. Suggested next review date: 2025-09-01.

Notes:
- This document is guidance and mandatory controls are denoted explicitly (approval thresholds, retention requirements). For regulatory or customer-specific requirements (e.g., certain enterprise DPAs), Legal may impose stricter controls which supersede this playbook.
